text:
sasha: quick heads up — noticed steady memory growth on the int8 canary with longctx workloads. KV cache keeps expanding instead of reusing pages. attaching profiler dump below. :clipboard:

carter: ugh. how big is the growth? can you share numbers + which branch this is on?

sasha: about +1.2GB over 15m on a 24k context trace (chat replay). 95p latency stable ~210ms, but resident set climbs, OOM risk if sustained. branch: runtime/slot-coalesce-int8-optim.

anya: do you see fragmentation or a steady increase in live slots?

sasha: looks like chain-of-pages growth — fragmentation at slot-level. slot_count increases (slots not reclaimed) even after prefix eviction. suspect compaction isn't running for int8 slots because of alignment heuristics. profiler snippet: 

```
KVCache: total_slots=1_024_000
int8_backing_pages=31_200
avg_slot_size=32 bytes
page_chains: mean_len=3.8, max_len=17
compaction_runs_last_hour=2
memory_growth=+1.2GB/15m
hotness: many pages show low reuse but pinned due to quantized_small_alloc policy
```

maria: correlated with evals: minor quality delta when running int8 on this model (perplexity +1.1). could be related but not huge. main issue is memory.

jordan: kernel selector might be favoring int8 kernels that require smaller alignment and thus create more micro-slots. compaction/slot-coalesce expects bf16 alignment. we changed the allocator earlier to improve throughput — maybe broke the coalescer for quantized pages.

anya: possible mitigation: temporarily force BF16 allocator for KV pages older than X tokens (cold pages) so they are coalesced, while keeping int8 for hot path. or run a low-priority background compaction that tolerates precision-specific layouts.

carter: can we do an immediate canary rollback of the allocator change? or flip a feature-flag to disable the quantized-small-alloc policy?

deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused: runtime/slot-coalesce-int8-optim (build 2026.03.18-rc3) — paused due to memory anomaly. See: https://ci.redwood/rollouts/9201 :warning:

infra-bot: Observability alerted: rts-canary-7 resident memory > 85% of instance for 3 consecutive 5m windows. AlertID=mem-grow-1951

maria: for accuracy tradeoff: if we fallback some pages to bf16, we might reduce int8-induced noise — but that increases token cost. need quick eval on small prompt set. I can run a 50-sample sweep.

jordan: another idea — compact-on-evict: when prefix eviction happens, try HIR->LIR compaction pass that merges adjacent quantized slots even if misaligned; cost is CPU but we can schedule during low load.

anya: agree. short term: flip feature flag to disable quantized-small-alloc (carter). medium: implement compact-on-evict for int8 pages (jordan + sasha). long term: update kernel selector to be quantization-aware for allocation patterns.

carter: I flipped ff/runtime.int8_small_alloc -> false on canary. monitoring now.

sasha: thanks. will post new profiler in ~10m. action items: carter(revert flag), jordan(compaction PoC), maria(eval accuracy sweep), anya(measure fragmentation telemetry).

maria: noted, starting eval now.

sasha: new snapshot after flag flip: memory growth stabilized, +40MB/15m vs +1.2GB before. still some chain_len spikes but no steady climb. we'll hold rollback for full revert if stable. :thumbsup:

carter: leaving canary paused until we get green for 60m. planning to roll back the branch from staging.

anya: I'll add a trace metric for page_chain_len distribution and a compaction_run_success counter.

sasha: thanks all. filing a short follow-up doc with root cause hypothesis and timeline.

carter: filing bug: https://issues.redwood/INF-3327 — "int8 allocator interaction with slot coalescer causes page chain growth on long-context workloads".

sasha: tagging owners in the ticket + will include profiler dumps.

jordan: once we have PoC, let's canary with a small background compactor enabled (cpu-limit 5%).

maria: eval results initial: perplexity delta reduced when we fall back older pages to bf16. will share numbers soon.

sasha: end.
